chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: The Honeydripper hit and Joe's switch back to clarinet
summary: Leon Rene recorded Liggins after hearing The Honeydripper at Jack's Basket, and Joe sold his alto for clarinet and soprano after Ory.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, what happened was, Joe Liggins was playing around here in a small after-hours joint called Jack's Basket, and Joe Liggins wrote that tune called "The Honeydripper." Every time he played it in this little club, people would give him a terrific hand or response for it. And Leon Rene happened to go in there one night, and he was listening... Rene had a recording company. And he said...this is a hunch: "I'm going to record these guys." And during that time, Joe Liggins was playing at this place,
Darensbourg - 188
this after-hours joint at night and selling sewing machines in the daytime -- he was a salesman.
Was he working as a single before this? Or did he have another group?
No, he had this deal, which was the same... The original "Honeydripper" was made with a (?), a bass, a tenor saxophone, alto saxophone and Joe.
Willie was playing alto with him then?
Little Willie, the blind...
Willie with the bad eye.
He had a bad eye.
What was his name? Wasn't it Jackson or something?
Willie Jackson. And this tenor man was named Jackson, too. But I can't think of his first name. Willie Jackson and...
You're not talking about Eddie Jackson, the tenor player?

No. The bass player was named Eddie Jackson with Joe Liggins! [LAUGHS] But I can't think of the name of this tenor man. Anyway, it was recorded with that group. And after Joe Liggins had gotten to be such a terrific hit, the minute that record hit... It was really something! People just lined up. It was just... And Joe
Darensbourg - 189
decided to add a guitar. That's when Frank came in. Then he decided to add a clarinet.
Oh, you played clarinet with him. I was going to say I thought you went back on saxophone.
No, no. I went back on clarinet.
You never did back on the saxophone, the alto, did you?
Oh, no. After playing with Ory for a while, I took my saxophone and sold it, and just started playing clarinet and soprano.
You still played soprano.
Yeah, I still played it. But I never played any more alto.
